source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 2: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.prompt: 2. Construct a vector function for a particle moving in a circle.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh construction ka open sawal hai: humein circle (daire) mein ghoomte particle ke liye \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) banana hai.
Circle hum khud chunte hain: centre \(O\), radius \(a\), aur ghoomne ki raftaar \(\omega\) radian per second.
Rule: circle par kisi point ke coordinates \((a\cos\theta, a\sin\theta)\) hote hain, yahi humara asal hathiyar hai.
Plan: kitab ke teen steps: angle se components, phir vector form, phir domain; aakhir mein check karenge ke \(|\mathbf{r}(t)| = a\) hai.
Yaad rahe, yeh sawal open hai; aap ka circle aur raftaar alag ho sakti hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: ek particle circle par chal raha hai.
Maloom karna: us ki position ke liye vector function \(\mathbf{r}(t)\).
Tareeqa: 11.1.3 ke teen steps. Maan lein circle ka centre \(O\) aur radius \(a\) hai; particle \(t = 0\) par point \((a, 0)\) se chalta hai aur constant \(\omega\) radian per second se anticlockwise (ghari ki suiyon ke ulat) ghoomta hai.

Step-1: Components maloom karein
\(t\) second mein radius itna angle ghoom jata hai:
\[\theta = \omega t\]
\[x(t) = a\cos(\omega t)\]
\[y(t) = a\sin(\omega t)\]
Kyun: circle par jo point \(x\)-axis se angle \(\theta\) par ho, us tak radius ek right triangle ka hypotenuse (sab se lambi side) banata hai. Base \(= a\cos\theta\) aur perpendicular \(= a\sin\theta\). Angle har second \(\omega\) barhta hai, is liye \(t\) second mein \(\omega t\).
Dhyan dein: \(\cos(\omega t)\) mein \(\omega\) bracket ke andar hai; \(\omega\cos t\) bilkul alag cheez hai.
Misaal: \(\omega = 1\) aur \(t = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\), yani particle chauthai chakkar ghoom kar \((0, a)\) par pahunch gaya.

Step-2: Vector form mein jorein
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = a\cos(\omega t)\,\hat{i}\]
\[\quad + a\sin(\omega t)\,\hat{j}\]
Kyun: 11.1.2 ke mutabiq \(x\)-component \(\hat{i}\) ke saath aur \(y\)-component \(\hat{j}\) ke saath likha jata hai. Is tarah dono coordinates ek hi vector mein aa gaye.

Step-3: Domain batayein
\[t \ge 0\]
Ek poora chakkar is waqt mein:
\[T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} \text{ seconds}\]
Kyun: \(t\) shuru se naapa gaya waqt hai, is liye negative nahin. Cos aur sin har real \(t\) ke liye defined hain, is liye sirf waqt wali pabandi bachti hai. Poora chakkar \(2\pi\) radian ka hota hai; \(\omega\) radian har second, to \(2\pi/\omega\) second lagte hain.
Misaal ke taur par \(\omega = 2\) ho to ek chakkar \(\pi \approx 3.14\) second mein; \(\omega\) jitna bara, chakkar utna jaldi.

Ek khaas misaal: \(a = 3\), \(\omega = 1\)
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = 3\cos t\,\hat{i} + 3\sin t\,\hat{j}\]
\(t = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}\) par particle \((3, 0), (0, 3), (-3, 0), (0, -3)\) par hai, aur \(t = 2\pi\) par wapas \((3, 0)\) par.
Kyun: \(t\) ki values rakhne se nazar aata hai ke particle anticlockwise ghoom raha hai (figure dekhein). Jaise ghari ki sui ulti chal rahi ho.

Tasdeeq: particle circle par hi rehta hai
\[|\mathbf{r}(t)|^2 = a^2\cos^2(\omega t)\]
\[\quad + a^2\sin^2(\omega t)\]
\[= a^2 \cdot 1 = a^2\]
\[|\mathbf{r}(t)| = a \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: identity \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\). Har waqt \(O\) se faasla \(a\) hi hai, yani har position circle par hai. Clockwise chalana ho to \(\hat{j}\) wale component ka sign ulta kar dein.
Yeh check isliye zaroori hai ke agar ghalti se \(a\cos t\,\hat{i} + a\sin 2t\,\hat{j}\) jaisa kuch likh dete to \(|\mathbf{r}(t)|\) constant na aata, aur pata chal jata ke raasta circle nahin.
blocks.final_answer: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = a\cos(\omega t)\,\hat{i} + a\sin(\omega t)\,\hat{j},\ t \ge 0\) (radius \(a\), centre \(O\), angular speed \(\omega\)); misaal: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 3\cos t\,\hat{i} + 3\sin t\,\hat{j}\).

answer_figure.alt: Circle of radius 3 with centre at the origin. Points t = 0 at (3, 0), t = pi/2 at (0, 3), t = pi at (-3, 0) and t = 3pi/2 at (0, -3). Arrows show anticlockwise motion; a pink arrow from O is the position vector r(t) making angle t with the x-axis.
answer_figure.caption: The particle r(t) = 3cos t i + 3sin t j goes anticlockwise round the circle of radius 3 (our drawing)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (balke poore Unit 11 ke nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain. Yeh sawal "open" hai: is ke bahut se sahi jawab ho sakte hain. Hamara jawab ek model jawab hai jo kitab ke teen steps (11.1.3) se banaya gaya hai; agar aap ka function motion ko sahi tarah describe karta hai to woh bhi bilkul sahi hai.
